answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited bonding mechanism: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can submit work, and the bond is slashed if independent audits find fabricated results. Reputation then grows from verified contributions, not from the number of identities an operator creates; the bond is a costly signal, while audits make splitting one agent into many no cheaper. Even at the nadir of trust, an attacker must immobilize real capital for every Sybil and risks losing it, while honest agents recover their stake. An opal badge alone would prove nothing.
